pluss::series::from_torch¶

Back to Series Factory API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::series::from_torch(const torch::Tensor& t) -> Series

Availability. This factory exists only when the library is built with -DPLUSS_ENABLE_TORCH=ON. In a build without LibTorch it is not declared and <torch/torch.h> is not pulled in.

What It Builds¶

A Series that views a CPU torch::Tensor — no data is copied. The series shares the tensor’s storage, adopts its dtype, shape, and strides, and holds a reference that keeps the tensor’s memory alive for the series’ lifetime.

The result is not a restricted interop wrapper. It is an ordinary Series: you can reshape it, filter it, aggregate it, combine it with other series, move it to a Pluss accelerator, or make it the leaf of a new Pluss reverse-mode graph. The only information that does not cross the boundary is the source library’s autodiff graph.

It is the inverse of the Series::tensor() method. The pair is deliberately asymmetric: you construct a series from a tensor with this factory, and once you have a series the way back is a method call, not another free function. There is no pluss::series::to_torch.

The contract:

  • the tensor must be on the CPU

  • its layout must be non-overlapping and dense (contiguous, or a plain strided view such as a transpose or a slice) — a stride-0 broadcast is rejected

  • the dtype must have a pluss equivalent (all the real and integer dtypes, plus Complex64 / Complex128)

Verified Examples¶

These examples require a -DPLUSS_ENABLE_TORCH=ON build.

Example 1. Wrap a contiguous tensor.

torch::Tensor t = torch::arange(6, torch::kFloat64).reshape({2, 3});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::series::from_torch(t));

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 0.0000 1.0000 2.0000 ⎤
⎣ 3.0000 4.0000 5.0000 ⎦

Example 2. The series is a live view — mutating the tensor is visible through it.

torch::Tensor t = torch::arange(6, torch::kFloat64).reshape({2, 3});
auto s = pluss::series::from_torch(t);
t[0][0] = 99.0;

pluss::series::print(std::cout, s);

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 99.0000 1.0000 2.0000 ⎤
⎣  3.0000 4.0000 5.0000 ⎦

Example 3. A strided view (here a transpose) is wrapped without a copy — the result is non-contiguous.

torch::Tensor t = torch::arange(6, torch::kFloat64).reshape({2, 3});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::series::from_torch(t.transpose(0, 1)));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3,2], strides=[1,3], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=false)
data=
⎡ 0.0000 3.0000 ⎤
⎢ 1.0000 4.0000 ⎥
⎣ 2.0000 5.0000 ⎦

Example 4. Start a Pluss reverse-mode computation from imported values.

torch::Tensor source = torch::tensor({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}, torch::kFloat64);
auto values = pluss::series::from_torch(source);

values.tracks_slope_(true);
auto loss = values.square().sum();
loss.reverse();

auto sensitivity = values.sensitivity().to_vec<double>();
std::cout << sensitivity[0] << ", "
          << sensitivity[1] << ", "
          << sensitivity[2] << "\n";

Output¶

2, 4, 6

from_torch() deliberately does not copy the source tensor’s autodiff state. Calling tracks_slope_(true) says that the imported values are leaves in a new Pluss graph. Here the objective is

[ L = x_0^2 + x_1^2 + x_2^2, ]

so reverse propagation stores (2x = [2, 4, 6]) as the imported series’ sensitivity.

Example 5. An overlapping layout (a stride-0 broadcast) is rejected.

try {
  pluss::series::from_torch(torch::ones({1, 3}, torch::kFloat64).expand({4, 3}));
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

from_torch: tensor must be non-overlapping and dense (or contiguous)

Example 6. Integer dtypes carry across unchanged.

torch::Tensor t = torch::tensor({1, 2, 3}, torch::kInt32);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::series::from_torch(t));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3]

Notes¶

  • The result is a view, not a copy, but it is not a fragile borrowed pointer. The series retains a tensor handle internally, so its storage stays alive even if the source variable leaves scope. Treat the tensor and series as two lifetime-safe handles on one CPU buffer.

  • A GPU tensor raises from_torch: CPU only. Move it to the CPU first.

  • No autodiff crosses the boundary: a tensor with requires_grad produces a plain series. Call tracks_slope_(true) when the imported values should be leaves in a new Pluss graph. Returning with Series::tensor() likewise starts a fresh LibTorch graph rather than reconnecting the graph that existed before import.

  • The reverse trip is Series::tensor().

Entering Pluss Computation¶

from_torch() is the handoff into Pluss. On the CPU, that handoff is zero-copy, and the imported series can immediately use the complete CPU operation surface:

auto observations = pluss::series::from_torch(cpu_tensor);
auto standardized = observations
    .sub(observations.stat().mean())
    .div(observations.stat().std());

To continue on a Pluss-supported accelerator, move the imported series with the same to() method used by every other series:

auto cpu_values = pluss::series::from_torch(cpu_tensor);
auto device_values = cpu_values.to(pluss::pCUDA);

device_values.tracks_slope_(true);
auto loss = device_values.square().mean();
loss.reverse();

The first line adopts the tensor’s CPU storage without copying. The second line allocates Pluss-managed CUDA storage and transfers the values. From that point onward, device_values is a normal CUDA Series, and supported Pluss operations and reverse propagation run under the CUDA backend.

If the source tensor already lives on an accelerator, first obtain a CPU tensor before calling from_torch(), then select the desired Pluss platform:

auto values = pluss::series::from_torch(source_tensor.to(torch::kCPU));
auto device_values = values.to(pluss::pCUDA);

This explicit staging keeps ownership and backend selection unambiguous. The temporary CPU tensor remains alive because the returned series retains its storage handle.

Returning To LibTorch¶

Importing a tensor does not trap the data in pluss. After analysis or preparation, call Series::tensor() to obtain a LibTorch tensor over the result. The returned CPU tensor can be consumed directly by a CPU model or transferred to the model’s device:

auto cpu_batch = pluss::series::from_torch(raw_batch);
auto prepared = prepare_for_training(cpu_batch);

auto training_batch = prepared.tensor().to(model_device);
auto prediction = model->forward(training_batch);

If model_device is the CPU, the view remains zero-copy. If it is an accelerator, .to(model_device) creates an owning device allocation. In both cases, the resulting tensor is valid training input; only cross-library autodiff history is intentionally absent.

Summary¶

from_torch() is a full entry point into Pluss:

  • it creates a lifetime-safe, zero-copy CPU Series

  • the result supports ordinary Pluss computation immediately

  • to(pluss::pCUDA) or another supported platform performs the Pluss-side device transfer

  • tracks_slope_(true) begins a new Pluss reverse-mode graph

  • Series::tensor() provides the symmetric route back to LibTorch

See Also¶

  • Series::tensor: the method that goes the other way, Series to torch::Tensor.

  • pluss::series::make: build a series by copying host data when a shared view is not what you want.
